newsitem.title: USA: Christopher to meet Syria's Shara at U.N..
newsitem.headline: Christopher to meet Syria's Shara at U.N..

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher will meet Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara in New York next week to discuss Israel-Syria peace prospects and Syrian troop movements, the State Department said on Wednesday.
The meeting will come during the United Nations annual General Assembly session when foreign ministers from around the world traditionally get together.

Washington recently sent Syria U.S.-Israeli proposals for reviving stalled peace talks, but there has been little sign of interest from Damascus, which accuses Israel of reneging on the principle of trading land for peace.

Syria in recent weeks has moved up to 12,000 of its troops in Lebanon closer to Israel's border, causing war jitters in the Jewish state. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday said the troop movements were an attempt by Damascus to pressure Israel into granting territorial concessions.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the Christopher-Shara meeting "will provide an opportunity to discuss all of these issues".

Washington has so far played down the troop movements. Burns said it was "obviously an issue that bears watching but we're going to, I think, also want to know what the Israelis think and what the Syrians think."
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross is currently touring the region, but the State Department says he has no plans to visit Damascus.
Burns also took a cautious line on the disclosure on Wednesday that Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai had approved a plan to build many more homes in a Jewish settlement in the West Bank.
"We will just first have to see exactly what this announcement is, what the timetable for construction is, if there is a timetable that exists," he told a news briefing.
"We want to, of course, talk to the Israelis first and get a better factual understanding of the announcement today."

The United States has long described settlements as a problem that complicates the Middle East peace process, a line repeated Wednesday both by Burns and by Ross, who was in Gaza for talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Washington says, however, that Israel and the Palestinians now have a negotiating forum of their own to resolve settlements and other contentious issues.
